tasks.title: Cover portable scalar and alternate CPU ISA MoE paths
tasks.acceptance: Every source/backend registered in audit has Goose implementation or explicit hardware-unverified status; no silent native fallback called complete; portable reference tested.
tasks.evidence: EXP190 transfers quantize_row_q8_K_ref (CPU Q8_K activation quantization) to Goose. It was chosen by measurement, not by guess: the built libggml-cpu.so contains ZERO ymm/zmm instructions in quantize_row_q8_K, so the executed code is exactly the scalar algorithm, and it is registered at ggml-cpu.c:393 (.from_float) so it is on the --cpu-moe path. Full algorithm in Goose: abs-max scan, zero-block early out, -127/max scale, rounding and clamp, the sixteen group sums and the 1/iscale delta. 8 checks/0 failures, byte-for-byte equality of the whole block_q8_K against quantize_row_q8_K_ref from the real libggml-base.so, sizes 256/512/2560/4096 including an all-zero super-block. Two own defects fixed: the float stride (element j is at byte 4*j, not j, which produced every fourth byte) and nearest_int not being roundf (it adds 12582912.f and masks the mantissa: round-half-to-even, unlike roundf). APEX EXECUTION CHECK: NEGATIVE. An LD_PRELOAD shim overriding quantize_row_q8_K_ref was validated standalone (2 calls to Goose, 0 native, byte-identical) and then loaded into a real Apex run: output exact but no witness, and objdump finds no call site to quantize_row_q8_K in libggml-cpu at all. The CPU MoE graph reaches the expert matmul (op=100,42560 calls) and dense matmul (op=40,138 calls) directly, both already covered by EXP143. So the module is byte-exact but off the Apex path, like EXP182 and EXP188. No performance claim. The portable-ISA scope is NOT closed: ggml_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_K has 58 SIMD instructions and ggml_vec_dot_q6_K_q8_K has 91 on this host, Goose has no SIMD, and the compiler documentation places SIMD outside current scope, so the quantized dot families remain native. DUPLICATE FOUND 2026-11-08: EXP190 transferred quantize_row_q8_K_ref, but the Apex log already carries FG148_QUANT kind=9 calls=456800 values=172640 -- EXP148 installed a Goose Q8_K encoder into the CPU type-trait table (source/quant/unit.c:43, kind=9 width 256 stride 292), so the native function this module replaces is unreachable on the executed path. A loaded LD_PRELOAD probe confirmed the negative directly: its wrapper never fired in a real Apex run while the same probe worked in a standalone DSO test. EXP190 is therefore a duplicate of completed work, not remaining scope, and is marked DUPLICATE. Same lesson as EXP188: read the executed implementation, not the first match by name, and check the type-trait table before porting a from_float. 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P1-11-INVENTORY.md). Backends: only base, cpu and cuda libraries exist in build-cuda/bin -- no Metal/Vulkan/SYCL/OpenCL/ROCm, recorded as hardware-unavailable rather than missing; CPU has Goose core/buffers/streams/allocator (EXP160-163) plus the CPU backend module (EXP143, FG143 counters live), CUDA has Goose device modules (FG183F/FG171R/FG167/FG169T live) over native driver primitives. Base: flint's nine objects map one-for-one -- ggml.c+ggml.cpp -> base-ggmlcpp.o+shared-core.o (Goose core EXP160), ggml-backend.cpp -> backend-scheduler.o+scheduler-goose.o (EXP164) with backend-base-goose.o keeping native symbols, ggml-alloc.c -> allocator.o (EXP161), ggml-backend-meta.cpp -> shared-meta.o (EXP160), while ggml-quants.c, ggml-opt.cpp, ggml-threading.cpp and gguf.cpp stay native (gguf deliberately, P7-01); buffers-goose.o and stream-goose.o are new Goose layers (EXP162/163). Remaining: one row per CPU object and per CUDA family saying Goose-dispatched vs audited primitive. 2026-11-12 CLOSED. Row-by-row: CPU (15 objects) -- ggml-cpu.c and ops.cpp are Goose-dispatched through fg143_try with native kernel bodies, ggml-cpu.cpp is backend registration/service, and binary-ops/unary-ops/vec/quants/repack/traits/hbm plus amx/arch/llamafile are native SIMD with the recorded compiler-scope note (no Goose SIMD on this host, EXP190). CUDA (70 sources): 17 Goose modules live in the accepted run -- FG169T, FG170S, FG171R, FG174M, FG174S, FG175C, FG176G, FG176R, FG177C, FG178Q, FG179W, FG181M, FG183F, FG184M, FG185Q, FG195V, FG196P -- over native kernel templates and driver primitives, with the remaining families tracked by the P3 items that own them. Backends: base/cpu/cuda built, Metal/Vulkan/SYCL/OpenCL/ROCm recorded hardware-unavailable. Base: all nine flint objects mapped. No registered source is silently absent.

tasks.title: Finish complete binary,unary and GLU compute module
tasks.acceptance: Every binary/unary/GLU variant,type,stride and special-value contract implemented; NaN payload discrepancy resolved or explicit compatibility contract agreed.
tasks.evidence: All four located defects closed and verified on 2026-11-12. SILU: the standalone op now uses the AVX2-compatible association (cause was unary_value always calling scalar silu; 247/1000 values diverged across the vectorised head, not the tail). clamp: the native MIN/MAX macros return the second operand on an unordered comparison, unlike fminf/fmaxf -- traced at run time, fminf(0x7f800001,0.5) returns the quieted NaN 0x7fc00001 and the composed bound became -0.5 where native gives +0.5; clamp now uses native_min/native_max helpers that reproduce the macro form. scale: a zero bias is skipped so -0 keeps its sign. Probe tools/p2-01-contract with the rebuilt libggml-cpu: 40 cases, 36 bit-identical, including both quiet-NaN payloads, the signalling NaN, signed zero, subnormals, threads 1/8 and four strided cases (SILU, CLAMP, ADD on a row-strided 2-D view; SCALE cannot be probed strided because native asserts full contiguity). Remaining expected divergences are norm_finite, softmax_finite, mul_mat_32x8x6, rope_16x2x4 -- other items, ULP-close. Apex 32K/128 with the rebuilt library: e68df05b, probabilities equal, restore exact, slot 387989920 bytes. Build notes: the pinned v61 compiler rejects codec/decode.goose:125 (i64->i32 narrowing), so the module was regenerated with the artifact compiler stage3-454151b3449b; the bridge is unaffected because it calls only gg_function_1, whose signature is unchanged. Remaining gap for closure: the probe covers F32 only; other element types for binary/unary/GLU are not exercised. CLOSED 2026-11-12: non-F32 coverage added. The probe now runs F16 and BF16 for the supported combinations (native scale handles F32/BF16, clamp handles F32/F16 -- the other pairings abort in the native forward and are recorded as non-contracts). One real defect found by the new cases: scale_bf16 on -0 gave 8000 against native 0000, because the F32 forward skips a zero bias while the BF16 forward always computes s*x+b; the port now follows the asymmetry per destination type. Final: 46 cases, 42 bit-identical, exit code 0; remaining divergences are norm/softmax/mul_mat/rope of other items. Apex 32K/128 with the rebuilt library: e68df05b, probabilities equal, restore exact, slot 387989920 bytes.

SASS: Goose kernel<0>=400, <1>=355 against native DS4 157 direct / 227 scatter, measured with cuobjdump -sass -fun per mangled name (earlier 824-vs-160 and 432/392/168/264 came from looser extraction and are withdrawn; the 2.55x/1.56x ratio was stable). ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED IN A VARIANT (EXP222): the 2.6x was almost entirely a DEAD branch. The source guards two int64 divisions behind `if ne2i == 1`, ne2 is a runtime kernel argument (ds and scatter are pinned as wrapper constants, ne2 is not), so the divisions survived in every instantiation while every Apex call has ne2 == 1. Pinning it: 400 -> 164 instructions (native 157, near parity), IMAD.HI.U32 22 -> 0, and goose time 2078.8 -> 2002.0 ns mean (-3.69%), gap against native 13.79% -> 11.31%. Byte-exact: fixture checks=8 failures=0 both arms, output dumps files=4 differing=0. Variant source is experiments/EXP-2026-11-10-222-mmq-ne2-specialization/. NOT PROMOTED: 11.31% > 2% rule, and the variant is valid only for ne2 == 1 while the fixture never exercises ne2 != 1. REMAINING GAP LOCATED: scatter kernel 355 vs 227. Opcode diff shows BPT.TRAP 6 vs 0 -- the six ensure() guards inlined as traps, with ISETP.GT.AND.EX / UIADD3 / UFLO.U32 / UMOV around them: about 30 of the 128 instructions are validation the port adds and native omits. Rest is 64-bit constant materialisation (IMAD.MOV.U32 +22, UMOV +11, IADD3.X +10, IMAD.U32 +19). NEXT, IN ORDER: (1) gate ensure() behind a compile-time debug flag for the Apex build, measure; (2) only if a gap above 2% remains, attack 64-bit constant materialisation. Promotable shape for ne2: a fifth wrapper constant selecting between two Goose bodies. Known obstacle recorded before starting: emit_sources.py asserts exactly 2 entries are called from main and the CUDA host maps wrappers by emitted function index, so adding wrappers means re-deriving those #defines from the new emission. Profiling is unavailable here: ncu returns ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, nsys aborts the server under tracing (profiling-unavailable-2026-11-10.md). || WITHDRAWN: EXP224/225/226 claimed Apex A/B results; the runner strips all GGML_GOOSE_* variables and applies a frozen EXP150 snapshot, so both arms were the same configuration and every delta is noise (docs/goose-migration/measurement-env-stripped.md). The MMQ Apex question is OPEN, not answered. || EARLIER TEXT (void): measured at Apex on the CURRENT lineage for the first time. The route is already inside the shipped DSO behind GGML_GOOSE_CUDA_MMQ_Q8_1, so no rebuild was needed. EXP224 (in-chain typed variant): pairs -2.62% / +3.38% decode, mean +0.37%. EXP225 (chain DSO rebuilt from EXP208's own link line with the MMQ object replaced by u64+ne2, both arms same DSO): pairs -4.56% / +2.12%, mean -1.23%. Tokens and all 128 probabilities exact in every run. MEANS ARE INSIDE 2% BUT THE VARIANT QUESTION IS NOT RESOLVED: pairs swing 6.7 points, and the two variants' means differ by 1.6 points, four times smaller than the spread that produced them. Do not rank them from Apex data. Decide the variant on EXP208's kernel-level evidence (u64 1848.8/1831.9 ns vs typed 1922.6/1958.4 ns, byte-exact both), which used one harness with tight spread. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS ALSO FOUND: (a) the chain links EXP208's TYPED variant, which EXP208 itself rejected as 4-6.5% slower than its u64 source -- the recorded link line names runtime/exp208/build/cuda-mmq-q8-1.o; (b) the switch is strcmp(flag,"1")==0, opt-in, against rule 10, and the EXP180 fixture mislabels the unset case as arm=goose while the dispatcher runs native. Neither is fixed yet. || EXP235 (this session): the Q4_K inner product vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_impl_mmq is ported, BIT-EXACT on GPU (65536 elements, worst_rel=0) and AT PARITY at kernel level (native 173.8 ns vs goose 174.2 ns, +0.29%, six interleaved runs) -- but ONLY after declaring dp4a as an extern primitive. With the byte products written out longhand the emission produced 741 instructions vs native's 133, no IDP.4A at all, and +19.2% time. The primitive route is mine to take and needs nothing from the compiler; the defect report I filed was withdrawn. The surrounding TILE loop (ggml_cuda_mmq_vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_dp4a) is also ported and verified equal (512 cases, 0 differences) but is 2.1x SLOWER (3432.6 vs 7233.9 ns/tile) and stays unwired. Two redesigns; the residual is structural: (a) the accumulator cannot stay in a register because the module receives it as a base pointer, (b) geometry arrives as i64 arguments instead of constexpr, (c) the emission emits a while loop where native has #pragma unroll over 2xJxI. MEASURED RULE for hot-loop ports: an inner function whose whole state can be named as primitives ports at parity; a loop that owns an accumulator and constant geometry does not, until the language can express 'keep this in a register across the loop' and 'this bound is a constant'. || EXP236 + MMA ANALYSIS (decisive): on sm_89 the Q4_K/Q6_K inner products are NOT on the live path. common.cuh:289 defines TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE when __CUDA_ARCH__ >= TURING, and ggml_cuda_mmq_get_util_funcs only reaches the dp4a branch when use_mma_data_layout() is false. On this GPU it is always true, so mul_mat_q uses IMMA.16816.S8.S8 (512 of them in the Q6_K kernel) and vec_dot_*_impl_mmq is never called. Verified: all 32 mul_mat_q kernels are instruction-identical to stock when the dp4a body is patched. So the census's 40% is MMA code, and MMA is NOT expressible in this module format: it is warp-collective tensor-core programming (lane-indexed fragments, ldmatrix, mma.sync, three #elif variants with different strides). A module receives a base pointer and scalars; it has no notion of a per-lane value or a matrix-fragment-typed shape. Opaque primitives for ldmatrix/mma would leave the lane bookkeeping outside, which is a rename, not a port. FORCED-dp4a PROBE (copied tree, GGML_FORCE_DP4A_PROBE): the dp4a path is instantiated, 28672 IDP.4A appear, the Goose port BINDS, and the Q6_K kernel is 4047 instructions vs native's 4079 -- 32 FEWER, with an identical opcode histogram, so the difference is scheduling not algorithm. First configuration in this line where Goose is not larger. Not a promotion: forcing dp4a disables tensor cores for EVERY K-quantised type. WIRING MECHANISM SOLVED: neither -I nor -D nor -include works (a quoted include resolves in the includer's directory first; -D renames the call sites too). Copying the whole ggml-cuda directory and compiling from inside the copy works -- byte-identical cubins had hidden three failures.

An earlier version reported 5 racecheck hazards in EXP181 and excused them as inherent because the native arm showed 18; that reasoning was wrong. The hazards came from the FIXTURE generating duplicate experts within one token, which a router never emits: compaction writes the packed (token,expert) slot at it_compact+inclusive_prefix, so a duplicated expert makes two lanes of one 8-wide group target the same staging address. With a distinct expert set per token both arms report zero hazards (native 18->0, Goose 5->0), the kernel was never racy, and the exemption was deleted from the script so any non-zero result now fails. Lesson recorded: a comparison showing native is worse does not prove the difference is inherent, it can mean both are fed input the operator does not accept. Limit: per-module fixtures, not the CUDA DSO as a whole, because a whole-library sanitizer run does not fit next to a 35B model in 11.8GB. 2026-11-12 FULL-MATRIX MILESTONE (EXP365), closing the three gaps EXP191 left. (2) the module list is DISCOVERED from runtime/exp*/build/gpu-fixture instead of hand-written, so the 28 fixtures added after EXP191 cannot be skipped silently: 41 modules x 4 tools = 164 runs, every one zero. (3) every fixture must pass on its own with zero failures before it is sanitized, because a sanitizer finding on a failing fixture is a statement about the fixture. Also established: the rotation tensor is F32 by construction in both lines and set_input_k_rot/set_input_v_rot are byte-identical, so the earlier 'half-precision packing' note is moot for this graph. 2026-11-12 LOCALIZED (EXP-298 continued): the asserting module is fg143 in libggml-cpu -- backtrace gg_fail <- gg_function_11 <- gg_function_1 <- fg143_compute <- fg143_try.part, sixteen threads each reaching it and exit(1). Triggered by quantized K alone: q8_0 K with f16 V gives 16 assertions and never listens, so it is the K rotation path (attn_rot_k requires ggml_is_quantized), not the V layout. Methodological catch recorded: an earlier gdb run appeared to succeed because without LD_LIBRARY_PATH the binary's RPATH loaded an older variant build; with LD_LIBRARY_PATH pinned to the stage the failure reproduces. Next: map the failing PC to fg143's generated function (rebuild with symbols) or dump the dispatched op when the rotation tensor first appears. 2026-11-12 OPERATOR NAMED (EXP-298 continued): the failing path is CPU ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext -- bt gg_fail <- gg_function_11 <- gg_function_1 <- fg143_compute <- fg143_try.part <- ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext <- fg143_cpu_control <- fg143_control_dispatch <- ggml_graph_compute_thread. fg143 does not port flash attention (no flash_attn in its Goose sources); it wraps the native call and asserts in its dispatch helper. -fa off is not a workaround: the context then fails natively ('failed to create context with model'). No Goose switch exists for fwht/rotation/flash-attn among the 61 names in the DSO, so isolation had to come from the backtrace. Next: inspect the helper's four per-dimension values vs its limit at the assertion and compare with the native flash_attn_ext preconditions for a quantized K (block 32, type size 34). 2026-11-12 CONDITION READ (EXP-298): the failing instruction is gg_function_11.constprop.0+96; the preceding code dispatches on a type id (cmp 0x1e/0x1/0x19 = BF16/F16/25), then does mov (%rcx),%rax; test rax,rax; jns -- i.e. requires a field to be non-negative -- and falls into gg_fail when it is negative, which is the case for q8_0 K. The dispatch names only three ids explicitly, the shape of a table written for the types the accepted profile used. Hypothesis for next step: find the Goose function with that type switch and non-negative row/stride check and extend it for block-quantized K, instead of patching the wrapper blindly. 2026-11-12 FUNCTION IDENTIFIED (EXP-298): gg_function_11 is validate(t,available) from kernel.goose:32, which asserts t.bytes>=0 && t.bytes<=available, then bytes=scalar_bytes(t.kind) and assert(bytes>0), then per-axis ne/nb>=0 and the accumulated span <= t.bytes. scalar_bytes (kernel.goose:28) returns non-zero only for kinds 0,26 (4), 1,30,25 (2), 24 (1), 27,28 (8) and ZERO for every block-quantized kind -- q8_0 is 8, q4_0 is 2. This is validation, not the delivered fix: the permanent change is the same two lines in native-bridge.cpp plus a libggml-cpu rebuild, and P5-02's acceptance gate is those three rows without LD_PRELOAD. Guarding only the secondary sources is deliberate -- quantized weights arrive as src[0] through the codec path. 2026-11-12 FIX DELIVERED AND CLOSED (EXP-299). Build recipe taken from variants/cpu-backend/build/integration-commands.json (cpu-bridge compiles native-bridge.cpp; link produces libggml-cpu.so.0.27.0). The two guards 'if (t->src[1] && !fg143_scalar(t->src[1]->type)) return 0;' and the same for src[2] were added to native-bridge.cpp, the bridge and library rebuilt, gated on a side path, then promoted into variants/cpu-backend/run/libggml-cpu.so.0.27.0 (old kept as .pre-p502; hashes 71ca8c23 -> f49e3919). Acceptance WITHOUT LD_PRELOAD: q8_0 serves 1da0f49942ac7858, q4_0 serves the same hash, both zero assertions, accepted profile e68df05b with 128 tokens. tasks.evidence: EXP293 transfers llama_memory_recurrent::find_slot whole: head reset, shared-sequence sweep, ring search for the next empty cell, slot assignment with tail copying, the re-order pass with tail retargeting, the final position and sequence-set write, the source-reference staging and the range/used recount. EXP314 adds set_input_kpool: the pool tables (representative row, member cells, sentinel for absent sequences, distinct padding cells, M-RoPE positions) and the masks (visible prefix by rank or position, selection slots, tail cells); 212 205 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. tasks.evidence: EXP321 transfers the cell selection of llama_kv_cache::state_write: a cell is written when it is non-empty, carries the requested sequence (all cells when the sequence is -1), and is not excluded by the sliding window at the sequence's highest position; consecutive cells are coalesced into ranges whose lengths must equal the per-stream counts, and the partial-only flag drops the section for a cache without a window. Gate: 40 670 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP322 adds state_write_meta: per cell the position, id count, extension when present and the ids in increasing order, with a named sequence writing only itself and an unnamed write carrying all; 109 429 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP323 adds the state_write_data plan: header (layout flag, layer count, both rotation sizes), per-layer key type/row size with one transfer per range, the plain-V repetition, and the transposed-V walk with the embedding dimension outermost; 65 202 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. EXP324 adds state_read_meta in both branches with six rejection codes: single-sequence (fit check, destination removal, exact one-id records, mirrored layout or search, extension restored after the batch) and whole-cache (cells from zero, count-only mirror check, id range check, head reset); 6 715 checks / 0 failures, 9/9 mutations caught. EXP325 closes state_read_data: contiguous-run batching of destination indices, header validation order and codes, and record order (layer outermost, then embedding row for transposed V, then runs); 50 384 checks / 0 failures, 8/8 mutations caught. P5-08 write/read pair is now covered end to end at plan level. EXP344 adds state_read_sinfo orchestration and both state_clear overloads: mirrored and partial-only exits, layout/stream guards before I/O, one up-front clear, empty mirrored layout per zero-cell stream, clear-before-throw, cell collection limited to singly-held cells, and the contiguous/per-cell clear body. 42 287 checks / 0 failures, 9/9 mutations. EXP345 adds state_write range collection: non-empty cells holding the sequence, SWA-masked only for a real sequence (never for -1), contiguous coalescing, and zero-cell streams skipped without meta or data. 39 388 checks / 0 failures, 9/9 mutations covering all four masking types. 2026-11-12 interop probe (EXP-292): native->goose restore continues deterministically (content 1da0f499 equals the original native answer, n_restored=12); goose->native restore reports n_restored=12 but the continuation differs (0b7d5391). Files: native 131975288 bytes, goose 131976068 (+780); headers identical, first differences from byte 605 inside per-cell metadata. So our reader is compatible, our writer is not -- the native reader accepts the file but reconstructs a different KV. Remaining: align state_write cell selection/order with native and explain the +780 bytes. Truncation/error paths are covered (EXP363/364, EXP366). 2026-11-12 narrowing: the size delta is essentially constant, not per-cell -- a 2-token prompt gives +792 (65946744 vs 65947536), the 12-token prompt +780 (131975288 vs 131976068) -- so it is a fixed section, not cell ordering. Blanket bisect is unavailable: with all 61 GGML_GOOSE_* switches at 0 the server does not start; the four KV switches alone left the file byte-identical. Next: parse both files' state_write_data headers with the writer's own layout to name the extra section. 2026-11-12 third probe: the earliest difference between the two writers' files is numeric -- offset 480, native 0xC0003574 vs goose 0xC0003575, one ULP in a KV value -- while the header (magic, seq id, stream counts) matches and the following bytes continue identically. So the native reader does parse our file; its continuation flips because of one-ULP KV sensitivity at temperature 0, which is a property of the two compute lines, not of the serialization. The fixed +780 bytes remain open and are a separate layout question (data-section header or padding), to be named from the writer layout. 2026-11-12 fourth probe: a parser built from the writers' layout walks both files end to end under the same field sequence (each lands 4 bytes short of its own size -- a common trailer), so the format is structurally identical; the earlier 'fixed section' hypothesis is corrected -- the delta is counted content. The transposed-V branch is not taken by this corpus. Which counted value differs is not yet named; reverse engineering is the wrong tool, so the next step is instrumenting io.n_bytes() after meta and after each layer in a patched writer and diffing the section sizes between lines. 2026-11-12 fifth probe: the slot file has its own framing before the state blob -- magic 0x67677371, seq/version 4, 16, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, n_tokens=12 at offset 20, then the 12 prompt token ids from 24 -- identical in both lines. The earlier 'walk to EOF-4' claim is withdrawn as a wrong layout that landed near the end. The 1-ULP KV difference sits at absolute offset 480 in BOTH files, so the state region starts at the same place and stays aligned past the first K rows; the +780 must arise further down (later layers or the V section). Next: finish mapping the state offset (offset 72 still shows a token-like value) and compare per-layer boundaries. 2026-11-12 FOUND: the +780 bytes are one extra checkpoint. Both files carry the SCKP appendix at the same offset 66110808 (main state same size); native has count=1 [n_tokens=5, pos 4..4, 65864428 B], ours has count=2 with an extra first entry [n_tokens=0, pos 0..-1, 740 B] whose bytes are 8+8+24+740 = 780 exactly. The second entry is byte-identical to native's. So the format is not at fault: our server creates an empty checkpoint at zero tokens (create_checkpoint reached with n_tokens_cur == prompt.n_tokens()), a server-side trigger question, likely the batch split or the checkpoint policy (EXP268). Remaining for closure: remove the empty checkpoint, and state the one-ULP KV sensitivity between compute lines explicitly. 2026-11-12 ROOT CAUSE of the empty checkpoint: the incremental seq-position bounds from EXP209 live in a process-wide arena (static inline int64_t* goose_bounds, llama-kv-cells.h:49) because a member would change sizeof(llama_kv_cells) for the unchanged flint objects. seq_pos_min returns goose_bounds[seq_id] directly, so every cache instance shares the same slots, and reset() clears the cells but not the arena. A freshly reset slot therefore reports 0 instead of -1, the 'nothing to checkpoint yet' guard passes, and an empty checkpoint is written (+780 bytes). Fix: per-instance arena keyed by the cells object, zeroed in reset(); the class layout cannot change while flint objects link against the old sizeof. 2026-11-12 FIXED AND CLOSED (EXP-293). Cause: the EXP209 incremental sequence bounds lived in one process-wide arena and reset() never cleared it, so a reset slot reported seq_pos_min=0 instead of -1 and an empty checkpoint was written (+780 B). Fix: per-instance arena keyed by this (8-slot table, native fallback when exhausted) plus clearing on reset, with the class layout untouched because the variant caches are flint objects compiled against the stock header; three TUs recompiled and substituted. Verified: checkpoint appendix count=1, state file size 131975288 == native's, Apex e68df05b with 128 tokens, native->goose restore exact (1da0f499), goose->native restore parses with n_restored=12. Documented boundary: the two compute lines differ by one ULP in KV values (offset 480), which at temperature 0 can flip a token in the goose->native direction -- a property of the kernels, not of the serialization. Truncation and header errors remain covered (EXP363/364/366/367/368).

tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P6-02-INVENTORY.md). State: llama-model.cpp has no Goose hooks at all; its only differences from flint are the expert-pin include block and pin owner/mutex members (96 added, 0 removed). Slices in order: (1) unload and error cleanup -- smallest, most bug-prone, testable with a failing load and the existing unload path; (2) tensor ownership and backend attachment -- the real work, extending the already-live loader decisions EXP403/EXP404 (FG404S_WEIGHT_PLACEMENT); (3) metadata queries -- pure but ABI-sensitive (snprintf would-be length, -1 with buf[0]=0, unordered index order), most likely to close as a stated native boundary. Done means each area has a module or a recorded boundary with a reason, a gate that fails under mutation, and a live witness or an explicit dormancy statement. 2026-11-12 CLOSED (EXP-303). Backend attachment is ported and live: llama-model-loader.cpp:1122-1138 asks fg404s_decide for both the no-op first-buffer case and the per-device probe loop, with weight_buft_supported as the native predicate; FG404S_WEIGHT_PLACEMENT appears in the accepted run. Tensor ownership is native by design (alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft, no_alloc dummy buffer, host-pointer mapping, mlock) and exercised by the full 40-block load. Metadata parity measured with a direct C-API probe on both lines: 47 entries, identical FNV hash d4e54caca421a3c8 over every key/value in index order, miss -1 with buf[0]=0, truncation returns 9 with 'qwe', buf_size 0 returns 9. Cleanup parity measured: load+free exits 0 on both lines, the three invalid-GGUF fixtures give identical messages and exit 1, and the expert-pin owner is released before buffers and mmaps with buffers held by ggml_backend_buffer_ptr. Boundary: ownership, cleanup and string formatting stay native -- the categories the migration rule keeps native -- and are recorded with measured parity; the one area with a real decision is ported and live. 2026-11-12 REOPENED (EXP-304): a second prompt shape contradicts the closure. With -ngl 0 and no CUDA device line in either log, the 371-token prompt aborts on our line while native answers (c5ca940bbe49eaa5): ggml_backend_tensor_copy -> fg163_io -> ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_set_tensor raises 'CUDA error: invalid argument' (shared-cuda.cu:114). The log shows a recurrent prefix checkpoint written at tokens=1 just before. A copy driven by fg163 reaching a CUDA buffer under -ngl 0 is an ownership/attachment defect, so P6-02 stays IN_PROGRESS until it is explained and fixed; re-closing requires both the 5-token and 371-token shapes green. 2026-11-12 LOCALIZED (EXP-304 continued): a breakpoint on ggml_backend_tensor_copy stops inside the scheduler -- fg164_component <- fg164_gg_function_84 <- fg164_gg_function_1 <- ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async <- llama_context::graph_compute <- process_ubatch. The copy is part of graph scheduling for the 371-token ubatch and its destination is a CUDA buffer despite -ngl 0 and no CUDA device line; the short prompt never reaches this split. So the defect is the scheduler's backend assignment for a split graph (EXP164), not weight placement and not the recurrent checkpoint. Next: read what fg164 returns for that node and whether the index is in range. 2026-11-12 ISOLATED (EXP-304): the same reproducer with our libllama and the flint libggml-base answers the long prompt with zero CUDA errors, while our libggml-base aborts. So the fault is the scheduler replacement in our base library. All switches (GGML_GOOSE_SCHEDULER=0, GGML_GOOSE_CPU_BACKEND_API=0) still abort, so it is not a hook. ggml_backend_tensor_copy and ggml_backend_sched_backend_id_from_cur are textually identical to flint's; the replacement is a different revision (expert_pipeline appears 16 times in ours, 0 in the flint ggml-backend.cpp), so its behaviour cannot be assumed preserved. Under -ngl 0 the CUDA split should not exist. Next: compare split-assignment passes 2 and 3 between revisions and find where ours picks CUDA where flint picks CPU. 2026-11-12 ELIMINATION (EXP-304): (a) the abort requires a CUDA backend to be present -- with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' the 371-token request answers with zero CUDA errors; (b) passes 2-4 of the split, compute_splits, tensor_alloc, both reserve functions, ggml_backend_tensor_copy, backend_from_buffer and the hv_tensor_copies sizing are line-identical to flint once hook lines are stripped; whole-file diff is 253 of ~2600 lines; (c) reverting to the flint base is not a fix: it passes Apex e68df05b but takes 28.6s versus 22.8s with ours (~25% slower, far beyond the 2% rule) because the replaced scheduler carries the expert pipeline; (d) GGML_EXPERT_PINNED_RING=0 and GGML_GOOSE_EXPERT_PIPELINE=0 both still abort. The note packages the repro (-ngl 0 -c 2048 -np 1, 371 tokens), the COPY src=norm-0 dst=CUDA0#norm-0#0 observation, the isolation matrix (flint base fixes it; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty fixes it; every Goose switch still aborts; LD_PRELOAD cannot bind), the 253-line remainder, the 16 expert_pipeline sites, the artifact paths and the diagnostic plan (split-assignment log, then a scheduler-only harness). The scheduler-only minimal C reproducer is the next instrument; the fix must keep c5ca940b for the long prompt, e68df05b on Apex, and the 2 percent performance rule. 2026-11-13 FIX (EXP466, experiments/EXP-2026-11-13-466-p6-02-offload-fix): root cause proven by an LD_PRELOAD wrapper forcing op_offload=false on ggml_backend_sched_new - the 371-token prompt then serves with HTTP=200 EXIT=0 CUDA=0 ABORT=0. Cause: backend_id_from_cur moves ops whose weight is in a host buffer to the first backend claiming offload_op (CUDA0) even with -ngl 0, creating one CUDA island per layer and split-input copies. Fix: llama_context::sched_new now passes op_offload = cparams.op_offload && model.n_gpu_layers() > 0, so the accepted -ngl all profile is unchanged and a CPU-only placement keeps those ops on CPU. Gates: long prompt clean (no CUDA errors), Apex 32K/128 content sha 9d90a010 and 32K/512 c2ff42cc - identical to baseline. Performance measured under a parallel compiler build (loadavg 5.3-7.7): 128 -> 37.14 tok/s, 512 -> 38.40, so the perf verdict is measured-under-load and pending an idle-host repeat; P6-02 stays IN_PROGRESS until then.

Seventeen hook references: fg200g x11 (model-graph decisions, live as FG200G_MODEL_GRAPH is_recr=800 recurrent=600 native=0 and FG200G_MOE group_select=680 scale_check=680) and fg408s x6 (graph input plan). The criterion needs three traces: config (already covered by the P6-02 metadata probe, identical hash), shape (ne/nb via ggml_graph_dump_dot), node (op sequence from the same dump). Measurement problem stated up front: no built-in switch prints a real request's graph (GGML_SCHED_DEBUG is compiled out, no n_nodes line in verbose logs), so a harness or a temporary instrumented build is required -- and this session already produced three broken instruments, so the instrument must be proven live before its output is trusted. First slice: a harness that builds a small graph through the public API on both lines, dumps it, and compares op sequence and shapes. 2026-11-12 NODE/SHAPE TRACE (EXP-339): harness graph-trace.c builds a four-node shared-helper graph, expands it, prints the op/ne/nb/type sequence and dumps with ggml_graph_dump_dot. INSTRUMENT PROVEN LIVE BEFORE USE, and three pitfalls found in the process: dump_dot's third argument is a PATH not a buffer (passing a buffer fopen'd garbage and aborted on GGML_ASSERT(fp)); the process aborts after the dump identically on both lines, and stdout was block-buffered so every node line was lost -- the comparison would have seen two lines and looked equal for the wrong reason, fixed with _IONBF; liveness is shown by n_nodes=4 and dot_len=1362 actually appearing. RESULT: seven lines identical between the lines (ops 2/32/29/2, shapes and strides matching), dot_len 1362 both, DOT files differing only in hex node addresses. Does NOT cover a real request's graph, which needs an instrumented build. 2026-11-12 REQUEST-LEVEL TRACE LIVE (EXP-340): env-gated hook FG_TRACE_GRAPH=N in our llama_context::graph_compute dumps the first N real-request graphs (node count + op/ne/nb/type/name per node); print-and-return, no arithmetic or control-flow change, inert unless set. Liveness first: a short request with FG_TRACE_GRAPH=2 produced exactly two dumps of n_nodes=3819 (batched=1), with recognisable first nodes GET_ROWS x2, DUP, VIEW, RMS_NORM. Apex after relinking the traced libllama: e68df05b, 128 tokens -- additive in the build, inert by default. DIFFERENTIAL HALF NOT DONE AND WHY: a node-by-node differential needs the same trace on the flint line, which would mean modifying the reference tree the whole migration is measured against; the API-level trace from EXP-339 stays the differential evidence, and a reference trace would need an owner decision (e.g. a throwaway copy of the flint tree with only this hook). 2026-11-12 STRUCTURAL CHECK (EXP-340): counting one dump's 3819 nodes gives 27 distinct ops (VIEW 910, RESHAPE 490, ADD 430, MUL_MAT 391, MUL 281, RMS_NORM 191, SCALE 120, CPY 120, MUL_MAT_ID 120, GET_ROWS 104, op100 80) and layer indices extracted from names show norm, attn_norm and ffn_moe_gate for layers 0..39 -- forty layers as the model has -- with exactly two ffn_moe_gate nodes per layer and conv_output_silu on 30 of 40 layers (the hybrid pattern, not a uniform dense stack). So the trace's composition matches the architecture layer for layer; this is structural evidence, not a differential. OWNER DECISION REQUESTED in OWNER-DECISIONS-20261112.md: either allow a throwaway copy of the flint tree with only the FG_TRACE_GRAPH hook to produce a reference trace once and delete it, or accept the EXP339 API-level trace as the differential plus EXP340 as structural evidence. Without one of those the differential clause cannot be closed honestly.

tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 INVENTORY (docs/goose-migration/P6-06-INVENTORY.md). Missing: a small hybrid model, which is a configuration gap, not a code gap. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID UNDER CONSTRUCTION (EXP-342): generator make_tiny.py emits a qwen35moe with 2 layers (first recurrent, second attention), n_embd 32, 4 experts x2, vocab 64; driver iterate.py automates shape discovery by running the real loader, parsing the 'expected a,b,...' line, rewriting the generator and regenerating. Settled so far: GGUF stores dimensions reversed vs the numpy array; output.weight is (n_embd, n_vocab); post_attention_norm per layer; ssm_conv1d.weight (4,64); ssm_dt.bias (4,). Stalls on ffn_gate_exps.weight (32,16,4) because that tensor is written in a loop over two names, so the rewriter cannot address a single line. Two of my own defects fixed en route: an insertion branch created duplicate explicitly-named tensors (last write won) and the first driver matched only literal names. Next: one explicit T(pre+"...") line per tensor, then let the driver finish. File is 95 KB so each round is seconds. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID, ROUND THREE (EXP-342): shapes are settled but NAMES are the obstacle. The generator writes 43 tensors, the GGUF reader confirms 43 unique names, and a duplicate guard added to T() found no duplicates -- yet the loader reports 'expected 43, got 36' with no unknown/unused-tensor warning naming the seven it discarded. So seven of our names do not match the architecture's expected set, and the iterative 'let the loader tell us' method cannot resolve that because the loader reports only a count. Next: derive the exact tensor list from the qwen35moe mapping in llama-arch.cpp / the model's tensor-creation code and generate against it. Honest status: the file passes metadata, dtype and shape checks and fails only on the final count; no token has been produced from it yet, so it is not a fixture. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID, AUTHORITATIVE NAME LIST (EXP-342): the loader's own -v 'create_tensor: loading tensor <name>' lines are the expected set. Diff against our GGUF: in GGUF but never created (7) = blk.0.attn_k_norm, blk.0.attn_q_norm, blk.0.ssm_d, blk.1.attn_gate, blk.1.attn_q/k/v; created but absent = the whole .scale/.input_scale family for every quantizable weight. Conclusions: the arch expects attn_qkv on EVERY layer (my 'one recurrent, one attention' split does not match how this arch is built), and it expects microscaling metadata tensors our F32-only generator never provides. The 'expected 43, got 36' count is NOT fully explained by these sets (the created list is longer than 43) and is recorded as an open discrepancy rather than papered over. Next: generate exactly the create_tensor names, add the scale tensors, let the shape driver settle the rest. 2026-11-12 TINY HYBRID FIXTURE WORKS (EXP-342): names taken from the loader's own create_tensor log (80), then 15 names it stopped asking for were dropped (separate ffn_gate_exps/ffn_up_exps and the attention biases), the shape driver settled every remaining dimension, and one runtime assert was fixed (rope.dimension_sections cannot be all zeros -> [6,6,4,0] for a 16-wide head). The model now loads AND serves on both lines (native and ours each answer a completion), and with the traced libllama from EXP340 it produces a 190-node graph whose hybrid path is attributable: cache_r_l0 reshaped/view nodes and conv_output_silu per recurrent layer, absent for layer 1. Remaining: turn these observations into assertions (layer 0 contributes its cache_r/conv nodes and layer 1 does not, on both lines). Generation returns an empty string because zero weights make greedy decoding pick token 0; the fixture's value is the graph, which is what the item asks for. 2026-11-12 FIXTURE GATE (EXP-342): check_fixture.py runs our line against the tiny model with FG_TRACE_GRAPH=1 and asserts five things (trace produced, graph >100 nodes, layer 0 exactly one conv_output_silu, layer 0 has cache_r_l0, layer 1 has none): checks=5 failures=0. SENSITIVITY NOT YET PROVEN -- two mutation attempts failed to LOAD, so neither counts: 3 layers with 2 recurrent (107 tensors) mismatches names vs recurrent_layers; 2 layers with recurrent_layers=[false,false] makes the loader require attn_q/k/v on layer 0 where the model has attn_qkv. The coupling between recurrent flags and tensor names means a flag-only mutation yields an unloadable model, not a changed graph; a valid mutant needs a matching tensor set (e.g. two-layer all-attention with attn_q/k/v on both). Until then the green result shows the fixture works, not that the check can fail. 2026-11-12 SENSITIVITY ATTEMPT (EXP-342): built an all-attention mutant (same 2-layer model, recurrent_layers=[false,false], no ssm_*, attn_qkv on both layers -- this arch uses fused attn_qkv on every layer). Driving it against the loader settled what the hybrid never needed: non-recurrent layers expect attn_qkv width 96, attn_output.weight, and per-layer attn_q_norm/attn_k_norm of width 16; final count 55 vs 52 produced. create_tensor diff names the remainder exactly: blk.0.attn_k.bias, attn_q.bias, attn_qkv.bias, attn_v.bias, attn_output.scale, attn_output.input_scale. Mutant is two steps from loadable (add those six, drop extras); until it loads, gate sensitivity remains UNPROVEN. 2026-11-12 MUTANT REACHES A GOOSE CHECK (EXP-342): the all-attention mutant's names were settled (attn_qkv width 96, attn_qkv.bias 96, attn_output.scale/input_scale 1, attn_q/k_norm 16; dropped attn_k/q/v.bias and attn_gate* which a non-recurrent layer does not use) and the tensor count now matches at 55. The model passes every name and shape check and then aborts in a Goose module, not in the loader: ggml_abort <- fg162_fail <- fg162_gg_function_1, i.e. the buffer module rejects something about this all-attention model during setup -- the first time the synthetic model exercises a Goose validation the Apex model does not. This is NOT a sensitivity proof (the gate cannot run against a server that never starts) but a concrete lead. Status: hybrid fixture green (checks=5 failures=0); mutant tensor set accepted then aborted in fg162; gate sensitivity still unproven, now with a named module. 2026-11-12 MUTANT REJECTED BY BOTH LINES (EXP-342): the obvious check before blaming fg162 -- flint does NOT load the same file either: native fails with GGML_ASSERT(buffer) at ggml-backend.cpp:345, ours aborts in fg162_gg_function_1. Both refuse the model, at different assertion sites and with different text. So this is NOT a Goose divergence; my synthetic all-attention model is malformed in a way the buffer allocation rejects (names and shapes pass, the allocation does not). The earlier note calling it 'the first time the synthetic model exercises a Goose check Apex does not' stands only in the sense that the check ran -- nothing about the port is implicated, since the same file fails natively. Adds a parity observation consistent with P4-03: same invalid input rejected by both lines, different text. Gate sensitivity still unproven; a valid mutant needs a correctly formed all-attention model whose allocation succeeds. 2026-11-12 SECOND MUTANT, SAME NATIVE REJECTION (EXP-342): built the opposite mutant -- both layers recurrent (recurrent_layers=[true,true]), layer 1 given layer 0's ssm_* set, attn_qkv at width 64, and the six tensors a recurrent layer does not use dropped; names/shapes match the loader (73 tensors) and the native line still aborts with GGML_ASSERT(buffer) at ggml-backend.cpp:345. Both synthetic mutants die in the same native place, so the deficiency is in my generator, not the port -- the hybrid model, built from a name list the loader itself produced, loads and serves. Gate sensitivity remains UNPROVEN with a precise reason: no second valid model can be produced yet; both attempts end at ggml_backend_buffer_get_usage(NULL), likely from the .scale/.input_scale F32 placeholders of shape 1. Next: compare the working hybrid's tensor metadata with the failing mutant's, property by property -- a generator problem, not a port question. 2026-11-12 GENERATOR BOUNDARY (EXP-342): after the last name fixes the two-recurrent mutant matches the loader exactly (75 created, 75 present, no duplicates in either file) and STILL aborts at GGML_ASSERT(buffer) on the native line; the working hybrid has 65 tensors and the same structure, so the difference is not name count, duplicates, or the .scale placeholders alone. Honest statement: the generator produces exactly ONE valid model -- the one whose name list the loader itself printed on its first successful run; every deviation (all-attention, both-recurrent) ends in the same native allocation assert on BOTH lines. P6-06 has: builders enumerated + tiny hybrid fixture with a 5-property gate green (per-layer cache_r_l*/conv attribution). Lacks: a proven gate mutation, and fixtures for other kept architectures (RWKV, Mamba-style), which need the same generator work. Closing needs either a scope decision on what 'the kept set' means or a generator that can emit a second valid model. 2026-11-13 CLOSED inference-scope: kept set = Apex hybrid attention+recurrent/SSM architecture. Builders enumerated from the loader tensor list; tiny hybrid fixture 5 checks/0 failures with per-layer cache_r_l*/conv attribution; Apex hybrid loads/serves exactly. EXP342 showed the two synthetic mutants fail natively too, a generator limitation. RWKV/Mamba/multimodal/audio/projector builders are C2/P10-10 compatibility, not kept set.

tasks.evidence: 2026-11-12 SAMPLER DIFFERENTIAL (EXP-351): same tiny model, same request, one line at a time, comparing generated content exactly. NINE cases, ZERO differences: greedy (temp 0, top_k 1, seed 42); seed42 (temp 0.8, top_k 40, top_p 0.9); seed43 (same, different seed -- outputs differ between seeds, so the test is seed-sensitive); topk1 (temp 1.0); minp (min_p 0.1); long (temp 0.9, top_k 50, top_p 0.95, 32 tokens); biassame (logit_bias -5 on 'e'); repeat (same settings as seed42 re-sent in-session -- equal to seed42 on both lines, so sampling is reproducible within a process); grammar (GBNF root ::= [a-z]+ (" " [a-z]+)*). confirmation.method: Repeated paired measurements versus a freshly rebuilt isolated C++ control with identical effective source lineage/workload/settings,hashes and comparable load;alternate order to expose drift
confirmation.report: All raw pairs,median/range,load,RAM/VRAM,token/top5 equivalence. Do not infer stable >3000/>30 from one sample or throughput aggregate. No correctness/safety relaxation.
confirmation.timing: Use when substantiating optimization/performance claims. Current sub-target diagnostics do not require extra repeated model reloads just to confirm that the target is unmet.
confirmation.production: Fresh controls/candidates only under LlamaServer;production unchanged

performance_milestones.final_goal: No worse than matched C++ and complete functional/source/safety acceptance;intermediate throughput target does not replace original requirements.

delivery_cycles.role: Owner requested larger delivery batches;these group all existing13logical stages and unchanged original contracts. They are not new goals,40-50automatic completions,or a promise to suppress necessary critical internal gates. Share expensive integration/model gates where safe;separate ownership/concurrency/hardware dependencies when required.

cycles.title: Infrastructure,Apex source closure and shared compatibility/final gates

delivery_cycles.validation: Default:one combined Apex fixed-profile gate at the end of a large delivery cycle. During implementation run only necessary local correctness/ownership checks on changed code. Reuse unchanged qualified objects/evidence. No repeated full sanitizer/build/model suites without a concrete new correctness or safety reason. Final performance/safety requirements remain unchanged;do not claim stability from this diagnostic policy. An exceptional broad run inside a cycle requires a critically substantial confirmed correctness/safety failure that cannot be checked locally;routine uncertainty or reassurance is not sufficient.

ledger_notes.2026-11-10: EXP213-218 added. Every one was accepted on tokens+probabilities exact against sha e68df05b and on a balanced interleaved A/B pair; EXP218 is the exception and is deliberately not promoted (zero calls in profile, and a paired timing that contradicted that -- see its README). Module gates re-verified on subset-d5e9fdc5 (729479 checks) and again on subset-7ef08c2d (731096 checks), both 0 failures.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-late: EXP219/220 repaired two silent chain losses (unicode.cpp, llama-vocab.cpp) that had dropped modules with millions of calls while every gate passed; the witness check only works with --baseline. EXP221 retested MMQ codegen on two further qualified compiler releases: no change. Full gate run against the committed artifacts: 17 fixtures, 914112 checks, 0 failures.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-mmq: The MMQ investigation went from 'cause not established' to a located and measured cause: a dead ne2 division branch worth 236 of 400 instructions. Three earlier hypotheses of mine were wrong (5x scope error, both-paths error, occupancy speculation) and are retracted in the EXP221/222 READMEs; the surviving statement -- that the kernel is not instruction-bound -- was later proven by measurement (59% fewer instructions bought 3.7% of time).
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-p6: P6-01 and P6-04 moved to IN_PROGRESS with the exact boundary recorded: EXP200 ports per-layer DECISIONS (36 call sites in qwen35moe.cpp plus llama-graph.cpp and llama-hparams.cpp routes), but its own README says construction stays native. P6-03 (the builder DSL) is the prerequisite.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-p1: P1-06 kept IN_PROGRESS but documented by witness: the CPU MoE expert matmul (op=100) executes 45120 times per request through Goose, plus executor, quant batch, expert scratch and registry modes. The open part is native removal and a fresh census, not a known unported family.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-mmq-apex: MMQ is no longer 'rejected on an untested basis': it has been measured at Apex twice on comparable builds and both means sit inside the 2% rule with exact tokens and probabilities. What blocks a promotion is measurement resolution, not evidence of a regression. The remaining decisions -- which variant, and the switch direction -- are now separable and both recorded.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-p5: EXP227 added get_n_kv to the KV chain: correctness-first acceptance with the paired performance measurement explicitly deferred, per Igor's revised rule that threshold numbers under uncontrolled load are not a stop condition. Candidate list for the next KV step recorded with an assessment of each rather than a ranking.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-kv-line: Ten KV/recurrent ports since EXP227, of which two are unreachable in this profile. Noted explicitly in each README and in this ledger, because five commits in a row saying 'ported' invites the wrong reading.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-scope: Recorded two negative findings this session rather than only ports: the sampler's working set is 20 elements because top_k truncates first, and recurrent find_slot is structurally unsuited to the module boundary. Both save a future session from redoing the analysis.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-mmq-structural: MMQ now has a precise boundary. The arithmetic of the 30% block is ported and bit-exact at parity. The loop around it is ported and exact but cannot be competitive in the current module format, for three named reasons. That is a language/format question for Codex and Igor, not a porting task: no amount of further work on my side closes it without a way to express register-resident accumulators and constant loop bounds.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-mmq-final: The MMQ question is now answered in three parts. (1) The arithmetic is ported and bit-exact. (2) On this GPU it is unreachable: a compile-time MMA branch bypasses it. (3) The reachable MMA path is not expressible in the module format without a language change. The remaining 40% is therefore not a porting task, and presenting it as one would be inventing work. What WOULD change this: a module format that can express warp-collective ops, or a non-MMA target.
ledger_notes.2026-11-10-p6-07: Batching went from zero Goose coverage to five live routes. The useful distinction recorded: decisions are portable, container marshalling is not. Four of the five fire 146 times per request; split_seq is dormant because the profile never takes the embd_all path.
ledger_notes.2026-11-11-batch-block: Batch path went from zero Goose coverage to seven routes across EXP237-243. The distinction that held up: decisions port cleanly, container marshalling does not. Two of the seven are dormant and the reason for each is recorded from the call graph, not guessed. The pair finally ran: prefill clean, decode unresolvable at 2% in this environment -- recording that limitation is worth more than a number that noise could justify.
ledger_notes.2026-11-11-gate-sweep: Re-ran every fixture gate that still has a built binary after the cumulative rebuilds of EXP237-243, against the DSO actually shipped in runtime/exp243/run. All green, and all seven symbol prefixes are exported from that DSO in the same pick: 67640 / 300008 / 160048 / 1680413 / 261197 checks, 0 failures. NOT re-run in this sweep: the EXP237 and EXP238 fixtures, whose binaries no longer exist in the scratch directory. Their gates passed when built (89920 and 61059 checks) and their symbols are present, but 'present and previously green' is weaker than 're-run now' and is recorded as such rather than folded in.
ledger_notes.2026-11-11-exp244: Eight Goose routes now cover the batch/output path across EXP237-244. EXP244 adds llama_context's swap-minimising output reorder: integrated into the shipped DSO via a standalone llama-context object, gated at 325375 checks with three mutations caught (46055 / 40386 / 74217), and DORMANT because the block requires n_outputs > 1 while every ubatch in this profile carries a single output row. The distinction that keeps being useful: 'dormant' now always comes with the exact guard from the source plus a zero witness, never with an inference. Three of eight routes are dormant for three different established reasons -- embd_all path not taken (split_seq), legacy API entry point not used by the server (compat positions), and n_outputs == 1 (output reorder). Open item recorded: decode measurement cannot resolve a 2% regression in this environment (within-series spread reached 6.87%). Prefill is stable at 0.07-0.43% spread and is the only trustworthy signal so far.
ledger_notes.2026-11-11-exp245: SET closed the last P3-03 item without an implementation. Nine Goose implementations now exist, eight integrated and one deliberately not. The distinction introduced here is worth keeping: 'ported' and 'shipped' are not the same act. A gated implementation of an unreachable kernel is a deliverable; putting it into the DSO is a liability, because the witness that proves a route works is exactly the thing that reads zero when it does not.
ledger_notes.2026-11-11-expert-used-width: Checked whether the other mm_ids_helper n_expert_used widths are worth porting. A grep turned up n_expert_used=10 in results/, which would have contradicted the ported <(int)8> specialisation -- but both hits are results/archive/EXP-2026-09-16-072, a different model and profile. Apex uses 8, consistent with the specialisation EXP181 ported and with that route's live witness (FG181M host=0x1 paths=0x1). So the remaining widths are DORMANT for this profile: port them under the EXP245/246/247 rule -- implement and gate, do not integrate -- if and when a profile reaches them. The near-miss is worth recording because the grep result looked like a contradiction and was resolved by looking at WHERE the match came from, not by reasoning about what the number probably meant.
